bundles.name: Assessment Frame, Subject and Scope
bundles.description: What this assessment is, who mandated it, what it is about, and where its boundary lies.
bundles.rationale: Every reviewed standard begins by fixing an object of assessment and a bounded scope before any criterion is applied: OSCAL names an assessment-subject and reviewed-controls, WCAG-EM makes scope definition and sampling the first two steps, and FHIR RiskAssessment requires a subject. Framing errors invalidate everything downstream, so identity, mandate, subject and scope are grouped as one top-level concern.

layers.name: Identity and Mandate
layers.description: How the assessment record is identified and versioned, and the authority and purpose under which it exists.

findings.name: Assessment record identity, granularity and versioning
findings.description: The identifier that authoritatively designates this assessment, the unit of record it covers, and how successive versions and supersessions are distinguished from independent re-assessments.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity, granularity and supersession are pure reference data carried on the record itself — identifier values, scheme names and pointers. Nothing is rendered, captured or attached here; any document that displays these values is produced by the conclusion or disclosure findings, so declaring an artifact would duplicate them.

findings.name: Assessment type, stakes and mandate
findings.description: The class of assessment, the party relationship between assessor and subject, the scheme or legal basis authorising it, and the consequence class its result carries.
findings.inline_only_rationale: These are classificatory and authority-bearing reference values that qualify the record. The scheme document, the legal instrument and the party records they point to are held and versioned by referenced sibling models, so materialising a local artifact would copy content this model must not own.

layers.name: Subject and Scope
layers.description: What was assessed, in what state, and how the assessed boundary and sample were drawn.

findings.name: Subject identification and assessed state
findings.description: Which object of assessment was examined, at which pinned version, configuration or state, whether it is an individual, batch, population or system, and where it was located when that matters.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The subject's own description, structure and lifecycle belong to its domain model; this finding holds only a reference plus a pinned state descriptor. Attaching a subject artifact here would reproduce target-owned content and create a second, divergent copy of the subject record.

findings.name: Scope boundary, sampling and generalisation limits
findings.description: What was explicitly inside and outside the assessed scope, how a sample was selected and sized if the whole subject was not assessed, and how far the result may legitimately be generalised.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Scope, sampling design and generalisation limits are declarative statements and counts that must be readable inline by any consumer before it trusts a conclusion. WCAG-EM treats them as reported steps rather than deliverables, and the sampled items themselves are registered as evidence references elsewhere.

bundles.name: Criteria, Method and Scale
bundles.description: Which criteria apply at which version, how they were examined, and the scale and decision rule by which results are expressed and decided.
bundles.rationale: OSCAL, XCCDF and Common Criteria all keep a versioned criteria catalogue separate from the instance that binds it, and all reviewed formats require an explicit method and result vocabulary. ILAC-G8 and JCGM 106 additionally require an explicit decision rule before a conformity statement. Binding, method and decision rule together determine whether a result is interpretable and reproducible.

layers.name: Criteria Binding
layers.description: Reference and version binding to the criteria source, and which criteria were selected, excluded or added.

findings.name: Criterion reference and version binding
findings.description: The catalogue, standard or rubric supplying the criteria, the version pinned for this assessment, the locator for each individual criterion, and any interpretation applied to ambiguous criterion text.
findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding deliberately carries only a reference, a pinned version and a locator. The criterion's normative text, structure and lifecycle are owned by the criteria catalogue model; embedding them as an artifact here would duplicate target-owned content and let a local copy drift from the authoritative source.

findings.name: Criterion selection, applicability and tailoring
findings.description: Which criteria from the bound source were selected, which were declared not applicable and why, and whether any criteria were added beyond the source and under whose authority.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Selection and tailoring are decisions about the referenced catalogue, expressible as identifier lists with justifications. Where a scheme publishes a reusable profile, that profile is a catalogue-side artifact referenced by identifier and version, not a document this model produces.

layers.name: Method and Execution
layers.description: How each criterion was examined and what must be preserved for the result to be reproducible.

findings.name: Assessment method, instrument, mode and coverage
findings.description: Which methods were used to examine each criterion, whether results were produced automatically, manually or semi-automatically, the depth and coverage applied, and the instrument, rubric or item set that operationalises the criterion.

findings.name: Execution parameters and reproducibility
findings.description: The tool, model or engine references, versions, configuration profiles and input snapshots that were in force when machine-generated results were produced, captured so an independent party can reproduce them.

layers.name: Scale and Decision Rule
layers.description: The vocabulary and scale in which results are expressed, and the rule that converts them into a decision.

findings.name: Outcome scale and result vocabulary
findings.description: The measurement level, bounds and favourable direction of any numeric scale, the controlled vocabulary for non-numeric outcomes, and how indeterminate, inapplicable, untested and error states are kept distinct from a negative result.
findings.inline_only_rationale: A scale is definitional reference data — bounds, polarity, level of measurement and an enumerated vocabulary — that must be resolvable inline for any consumer to interpret a score. The authoritative scale and code-system documents are held by the vocabulary registry this model aligns to, so producing a local artifact would fork a governed vocabulary.

findings.name: Decision rule, thresholds and uncertainty handling
findings.description: The rule that converts scored or determined values into a conformity or grade decision, the cut scores, acceptance limits and guard bands it uses, how uncertainty is accounted for beforehand, and the conditions under which the assessment must abstain.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The decision rule must be machine-readable inline so a consumer can re-derive the conclusion from the recorded values. Where the rule is published by a scheme or laboratory quality system, it is referenced by identifier and version; enforcing or executing the rule against live systems belongs to the referenced enforcement model, not here.

bundles.name: Evidence and Observation
bundles.description: What was relied on, how it links to criteria, whether it is sound, and what was actually observed.
bundles.rationale: OSCAL separates observations carrying evidence from findings that judge criteria; SP 800-53A ties evidence to determination statements; EARL requires a subject and a test behind every result. Evidence handling is therefore a distinct top-level concern from determination, and its quality qualifiers decide whether a conclusion is defensible.

layers.name: Evidence Corpus
layers.description: The evidence items relied on, their linkage to criteria, and their quality and admissibility.

findings.name: Evidence items and criterion linkage
findings.description: The discrete evidence items relied on, their types, the criterion or determination statement each supports or contradicts, and the times at which each was created, collected and received.

findings.name: Evidence quality, admissibility and reuse limits
findings.description: Whether each item is authentic and unaltered since collection, whether it is still current for the assessed state, which offered evidence was rejected or down-weighted, and which items carry confidentiality or personal-data constraints limiting reuse.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Quality qualifiers are assertions attached to evidence already registered by the linkage finding: digests, expiry dates, exclusion reasons and sensitivity codes. The evidence bytes are held by the referenced custody model and the artifact for them is declared once, so restating them here would create a second registration of the same object.

layers.name: Observation and Measurement
layers.description: Raw observed results with distinct event and recording times, and the uncertainty and traceability that qualify quantitative values.

findings.name: Observation records, actors and timing
findings.description: The raw result observed or returned for each check before judgement is applied, the actor or device that produced it, the separation of the time the observed condition held from the time the observation was recorded, and the place of observation where it matters.

findings.name: Measurement uncertainty and traceability
findings.description: The stated uncertainty of each quantitative result and how it was evaluated, the quantity, unit and reference scale each value belongs to, and the calibration or reference standard the measurement is traceable to.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Uncertainty statements, units and traceability pointers are declared values carried alongside each quantitative result. Calibration certificates and the traceability chain are produced and maintained by the referenced metrology model; this model neither runs calibration programmes nor issues those certificates, so it declares no artifact for them.

bundles.name: Determination, Scoring and Conclusion
bundles.description: Criterion-level verdicts and scores, their aggregation into a composite result, and the stated conclusion with its validity.
bundles.rationale: ISO/IEC 17000 distinguishes determination from review and from decision; OSCAL distinguishes observations from findings; XCCDF distinguishes rule-results from a scored TestResult. This bundle keeps criterion-level determination, aggregation and the accountable conclusion as separate, traceable steps rather than collapsing them into a single verdict.

layers.name: Criterion-Level Outcomes
layers.description: Per-criterion verdicts with rationale and locators, and the raw and normalised scores that accompany them.

findings.name: Criterion verdict, rationale and locator
findings.description: The outcome value assigned to each criterion from the bound vocabulary, the reasoning connecting cited evidence to that outcome, the severity or materiality of negative outcomes, and where in the subject each negative outcome occurs.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Criterion outcomes are structured values keyed to criterion identifiers and must be queryable, sortable and diffable as data rather than read out of a rendered document. The report that presents them to a reader is declared once by the conclusion finding, which keeps a single authoritative rendition.

findings.name: Criterion scores and normalisation
findings.description: The raw score recorded for each criterion against its maximum, how raw scores are normalised or rescaled before aggregation, and which scale definition version each recorded score refers to.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Scores are numeric data bound to a scale reference and must be recomputable and comparable across records. QTI keeps outcome variables as declared data separate from results reporting, and this finding follows that separation; the rendered scorecard is declared by the aggregation finding.

layers.name: Composite Result, Conclusion and Validity
layers.description: How criterion results roll up, what conclusion is stated and by whom, and for how long and under what conditions it holds.

findings.name: Aggregation model and composite result
findings.description: The scoring or aggregation model that combines criterion results, the weights and precedence rules it applies, the form in which the composite is expressed, and how it is computed when some criteria are untested or indeterminate.

findings.name: Conclusion statement, authority and qualification
findings.description: The stated conclusion and its form, the actor accountable for it and whether the decision was separated from the determination work, the qualifications, adverse opinions or dissent attached, and what the conclusion entitles or obliges.

findings.name: Validity window, conditions and confidence
findings.description: From when until when the conclusion is asserted to hold, the conditions whose breach voids it early, the surveillance or re-assessment needed to keep it current, and the confidence or assurance level claimed.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Validity is expressed as timestamps, conditions and a claimed assurance level that consumers must evaluate programmatically before relying on a conclusion. Surveillance activities themselves are executed under the referenced scheme or programme model, and any certificate that carries these dates is issued by the attestation model.

bundles.name: Assurance of the Assessment Itself
bundles.description: Whether the people, tools and instrument behind the result can be relied on.
bundles.rationale: EU law makes legal effect depend on the designation of the body rather than the quality of the method; ILAC and ISO/IEC 17025 make impartiality and competence preconditions of a statement of conformity; and the AERA/APA/NCME Standards make validity, reliability and fairness foundational. Assurance of the assessor and the instrument is therefore a separate concern from the result itself.

layers.name: Assessor and Independence
layers.description: Who performed the assessment, in what roles, with what competence and authorisation, and under what declared conflicts.

findings.name: Assessor identity, roles and contribution
findings.description: Which persons, teams, bodies or automated agents performed the assessment, how the roles of collecting, determining, reviewing and deciding were distributed, and which parts of the result are attributable to which agent.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Assessor identity and role assignment are references into the party model plus PROV-style attribution links. Personnel records, employment status and organisational structure are maintained by that referenced model, so this finding holds pointers and role codes only.

findings.name: Competence, authorisation and impartiality
findings.description: The competence, qualification or accreditation supporting each assessor's participation, the designated scope within which the assessing body may act, declared relationships that could impair impartiality, and what the assessment explicitly does not entitle the assessor to assert.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Competence, accreditation and designation are asserted and maintained by accreditation authorities and party registries; this finding carries their identifiers, validity and scope plus a locally authored conflict declaration. Reproducing accreditation certificates here would copy content owned by the accreditation registry and risk asserting a status this model cannot verify.

layers.name: Quality Control and Instrument Quality
layers.description: Review and moderation of this assessment, and the standing evidence that the instrument measures what the conclusion claims, reliably and fairly.

findings.name: Review, moderation and rater agreement
findings.description: The independent review, second marking or moderation performed before finalisation, the inter-rater or inter-tool agreement measured against a threshold, and how disagreements between assessors or tools were resolved.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Review is a function of this assessment recorded as structured events, statistics and outcomes attached to the record. ISO/IEC 17000 treats review as an internal function preceding the decision rather than a deliverable, and the review's visible output is carried in the assessment report already declared.

findings.name: Instrument validity, reliability and fairness evidence
findings.description: The standing evidence that the instrument measures what the conclusion claims, that its results are precise and repeatable, that bias and accessibility barriers across subject groups have been checked, and the populations or contexts for which it is not validated.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, Disclosure and Interoperability
bundles.description: How the record moves through its states, how it is corrected and challenged, who may see what, how long it is kept, and how it projects into external formats.
bundles.rationale: OSCAL requires record identity and last-modified to change on every content change; FHIR supplies an explicit status vocabulary including entered-in-error; the AERA/APA/NCME Standards give test takers rights that imply an appeal route; EU law limits who may publish a result with legal effect; and EARL, XCCDF, OSCAL and QTI all define incompatible result vocabularies that must be crosswalked deliberately.

layers.name: Record Lifecycle
layers.description: States and transitions of the assessment record, and how it is corrected, challenged and superseded.

findings.name: Assessment state and transitions
findings.description: The states an assessment record may occupy and the vocabulary defining them, the permitted transitions with their actors and preconditions, what becomes immutable at finalisation, and how a record that should never have existed is marked without erasing its history.
findings.inline_only_rationale: States and transitions are control data on the record, consumed by callers to decide whether a conclusion may be relied on. The platform's change history and access log are owned by the referenced audit model, so this finding records status and transition times without producing or owning an audit artifact.

findings.name: Correction, appeal and supersession
findings.description: When an amendment is required rather than a new assessment, how the subject or a relying party may challenge the conclusion and within what period, how the outcome of a challenge is reflected, and how the chain from the original to the currently effective conclusion is navigated.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Correction and supersession are expressed as reason codes, pointers and flags that let a consumer resolve the currently effective conclusion. Appeal case files, hearings and their procedural conduct are handled by the referenced dispute or case-management model; this finding retains only the reference and the recorded outcome.

layers.name: Disclosure and Retention
layers.description: Who may see which part of the record, what is redacted before release, and how long each part is kept before disposition is referred onward.

findings.name: Disclosure classification and redaction
findings.description: The disclosure class applying separately to the conclusion, the scores and the underlying evidence, the terms under which the assessment may be published or cited, what must be redacted before external release and who approves it, and whether a conclusion may be released without its evidence.

findings.name: Retention class and disposition referral
findings.description: The retention class and trigger applying to each part of the record, which policy and system execute destruction or transfer when retention ends, and how a legal hold or open appeal suspends disposition.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Retention here is a declared classification, a trigger event and a pointer to the owning records-management policy, plus a record that the referral was made. Setting periods and executing destruction, transfer or erasure — and issuing any destruction certificate — belong to that referenced model, so producing an artifact here would assert ownership of disposition this model does not hold.

layers.name: Interoperability
layers.description: Projection into external assessment reporting formats and binding of the vocabularies, units and languages used.

findings.name: External alignment and vocabulary binding
findings.description: Which external assessment reporting formats this record must project into, how local outcome values map into each target vocabulary and where that mapping loses information, which code systems, units and language tags are bound at which versions, and what is claimed as conformance to an external standard.

model.name: Attestation / Credential
model.purpose: Represent issuer-asserted claims with durable identity, evidence, validity, status, securing and purpose-bound presentation while remaining independent of storage and interface format.
model.scope_statement: Owns credential class and issued-instance identity, claim and schema references, issuer, subject and holder role bindings, issuance evidence, validity, status and lifecycle, secured representations, credential-specific verification evidence, presentations, disclosure manifests, interoperability mappings and governed retention. Party identity, issuer mandate, subject profile, source evidence, keys, permission-bearing grants, trust policy, authorization decisions and generic audit logs remain external.
in_scope: Credential and attestation definitions, instance and representation identity, typed claims, schema, vocabulary, issuer authority reference, subject binding and issuance evidence
Validity and terms, status method and freshness, suspension, revocation, expiry, renewal, correction, supersession, secured representations and verification results
Presentation requests, disclosures, holder binding, privacy and correlation, format mappings, role views, access, retention, provenance and safe agent operations
out_of_scope: Person, organization, issuer, subject, holder, verifier, mandate, source evidence, key, trust policy, permit grant, authorization decision or audit-log master lifecycle
Implementing proof, signature, wallet, PKI path, status-list or presentation-protocol algorithms and storing private keys or undisclosed secrets
Universal claim truth, issuer trust, identity proofing, authentication, authorization, eligibility, legal effect or certified cross-format equivalence

boundary_notes.distinction: The credential owns the issuer's claim expression and references evidence; source observations and evidence artifacts keep their own identity and provenance.
Issuer, subject, holder and verifier identities and public key references remain external; credential verification is not authentication by itself.
A licence or permit credential may evidence an external grant, but its authenticity and status do not themselves make an authorization decision.
Generic proof artifacts and verification methods remain external or reusable mixins; this model binds them to credential claim, validity, status and presentation context.
This model records credential-specific presentations and verification evidence, while wallet inventory and generic append-only audit execution remain external.

functions.name: Define credential class and profile
functions.description: Establish claim vocabulary, schema, required evidence, issuer authority, validity, status and representation rules.
preconditions: namespace, semantic definitions, issuer mandate, privacy and interoperability validate
effects: a versioned class is available without issuing an instance

functions.name: Issue attestation or credential
functions.description: Create an immutable issued assertion and representations after an authorized evidence-backed decision.
outputs: issued credential revision and issuance event
preconditions: issuer authority, subject binding, schema, evidence, validity, status method and expected serial validate
effects: issuer record and permitted holder copy are created with provenance

functions.name: Deliver, accept and custody holder copy
functions.description: Transfer a representation to a holder or wallet and record receipt without transferring issuer authority.
preconditions: holder authority, channel, integrity, privacy and recovery policy validate
effects: a controlled copy becomes available to the holder

functions.name: Publish or refresh status
functions.description: Issue a privacy-aware, time-qualified credential status assertion or list update.
preconditions: authority, method, purpose, index, freshness, signing and privacy validate
effects: relying parties can obtain current source-qualified standing

functions.name: Suspend, reinstate, revoke, expire, renew or supersede
functions.description: Append a credential lifecycle event and derived state while preserving earlier claims and representations.
preconditions: transition guard, authority, effective time, status publication, notification and lineage validate
effects: current standing changes without rewriting issued history

functions.name: Create presentation request
functions.description: Record verifier, purpose, audience, requested claims or predicates, formats, nonce and expiry.
preconditions: verifier identity, authority, minimization, client binding, nonce and expiry validate
effects: a bounded disclosure request becomes attributable

functions.name: Derive and present credential
functions.description: Create a request-bound presentation with permitted disclosure and optional holder binding.
preconditions: credential status, request, nonce, audience, holder binding, minimization and format validate
effects: the verifier receives purpose-bound evidence without mutating the credentials

functions.name: Verify credential or presentation
functions.description: Record schema, proof, key, path, status, time and request-binding checks and structured outcome.
preconditions: algorithms, canonicalization, keys, status freshness, time, trust input and policy version validate
effects: technical outcome becomes attributable without making an authorization decision

functions.name: Project or transform loss-aware
functions.description: Map a credential to another representation or sector profile with explicit omissions and semantic conflicts.
preconditions: source and target versions, issuer, subject, claims, validity, proof, status and round-trip class validate
effects: consumer receives a traceable representation with visible limitations

functions.name: Correct, retain, dispose and audit
functions.description: Create a successor correction or execute authorized retention and disposition while preserving required lineage.
preconditions: expected head, issuer authority, legal hold, subject rights, minimum tombstone and post-write checks validate
effects: current data changes without erasing accountable issuance and status history

policies: Credential authenticity, integrity, current status, issuer authority, claim truth, subject control, authorization, eligibility and business acceptance are separate attributable judgments.
Holder custody does not make the holder the subject or issuer, and a licence or permit credential may evidence but does not replace the external permission-bearing grant.
Issued claims are immutable; correction, renewal, suspension, revocation and supersession append events and lineage and never silently rewrite issuer history.

Agents may perform allowlisted reversible validation and projection, but issuance, revocation, broader disclosure, trust-policy change and destructive disposition require delegated authority and policy-defined confirmation.

coverage.claim: Covers the issued attestation/credential aggregate from class and claim semantics through issuance, validity, status, securing, presentation, verification, loss-aware projection and governed disposition, grounded in eleven tier-1 W3C, IETF, OpenID Foundation and NIST sources whose citations are topically consistent with the findings that invoke them. boundaryDecision.rationale: Two axes must be separated. On the record plane, a frozen registry value such as standalone-mm classifies how the entry is stored and governed in the registry, not what the subject is; it is never a subject-model entry kind. The pack ships frozen_context as an empty object, so the registry value could not be re-read here and its cross-check is held. On the subject-model plane, the declared 'mixin' is not defensible against the provider's own evidence: the model mints and canonicalizes issued-instance identity (authoritative issuer plus credential identifier), owns an append-only lifecycle with activate/suspend/revoke/renew/correct/supersede events, defines disposition authority, legal hold, tombstones, an artifact identity priority ladder and seven steward roles. A mixin is a reusable trait attached to a host entity and owns no independent identity, retention authority or delete policy. 'aggregate' is preferred over 'entity' because credential class, typed claims, secured representations, proofs, status entries, presentations, disclosure manifests and receipts are non-independent parts governed under a single root, and the provider's own coverage claim already calls the subject 'an issued attestation and credential aggregate'. Status is reclassified rather than split, but presentation and disclosure ownership is recorded as the leading split candidate because a presentation binds a set of credentials from possibly several issuers and cannot canonicalize under one credential identifier.

decisions.rationale: The scope statement, canonicalization rules, artifact identity ladder, CRUD delete policy and steward roles all describe a root that owns instance identity and retention authority; a mixin owns none of these, and the provider's own coverage claim already names the subject an aggregate.

decisions.concept: Aggregate root = issued credential instance qualified by issuing authority
decisions.rationale: Canonicalization by authoritative issuer plus credential identifier, with explicit refusal of subject name, issuer serial alone, timestamp, claim values or proof digest as identity, is internally consistent across canon_and_patch, artifact_rules and every artifact identity_strategy, and matches SRC-001 and SRC-005 identity practice.

decisions.concept: Presentation, disclosure manifest and receipt ownership inside the credential aggregate
decisions.rationale: A presentation carries its own identifier, holder binding, proof and a credential set that may span issuers, so it cannot canonicalize under the mandated {credential-id} serial rule; the boundary is retained for the draft but flagged for a split decision once relation rows exist.

decisions.concept: Verifier-authored presentation request as an owned function
decisions.rationale: create-presentation-request records verifier, purpose, audience, nonce and expiry, which are authored outside the credential aggregate; retaining it risks duplicating a Verifier or Request model, so it is kept as a reference-only record pending cross-model adjudication.

decisions.concept: Externalization of issuer, subject, holder, key, mandate, grant, decision and audit masters
decisions.rationale: out_of_scope, the five boundary_notes, the composition checklist row and the stated policies agree without contradiction, and this externalization is what keeps credential authenticity from collapsing into authorization, which is the central risk for this subject.

decisions.concept: Separation of technical verification from claim truth, issuer trust and authorization
decisions.rationale: This distinction is carried consistently by a dedicated finding with an explicit non-authorization marker, a service-layer policy, an adversarial check and a declared conflict, and is directly supported by SRC-001 and SRC-009; it is the strongest and most defensible part of the result.

decisions.concept: Three-question template with rotated kind labels
decisions.rationale: All 24 findings carry the same three question stems and the kind values rotate mechanically, so an identity-shaped stem is labelled 'ownership' and the histogram is a flat 3 per kind with validation at 6; the labels are generation artifacts and must not be published as evidence of analytic coverage.

decisions.disposition: rejected - downgrade spatial and interoperability to partial

decisions.concept: Legal effect, accreditation and recognition finding source support
decisions.rationale: The finding cites only SRC-001, SRC-005 and SRC-009, none of which establish legal effect, issuer accreditation or mutual recognition, so no legal-effect assertion may be published until a legal or conformity-assessment authority is added.

decisions.concept: Source version pins including RFC 9901 and four co-dated W3C Recommendations
decisions.rationale: A no-tools audit cannot confirm that SD-JWT is RFC 9901 dated November 2025, that SRC-001 to SRC-004 all carry the 15 May 2025 Recommendation date, or that RFC 6960 is updated by RFC 8954 and RFC 9654; each pin must be re-resolved against the live source before promotion.

model.name: Position
model.purpose: Model the position as a durable, addressable organizational construct that exists independently of any occupant: the work assigned by competent authority, classified, placed, funded, requirement-bearing and lifecycle-governed, so agents can create, inspect, classify, staff and retire positions without conflating them with people, jobs or contracts.
model.scope_statement: In scope is everything that is true of a position while it is vacant. A position is the bundle of duties and responsibilities assigned by competent authority (5 CFR 511.101) and modelled as org:Post, which W3C defines as a position existing independently of the person or persons filling it. The model owns identity, titling, duty content, occupational and grade classification, structural placement and reporting, location and work arrangement, capacity (FTE/headcount) and funding, requirements and essential functions, delegated and prescribed authority, risk/screening designations, working conditions, lifecycle and effective-dated change, governance and evidence, and outbound interoperability. It does not own the person, the occupancy relationship, the employment contract, the recruiting workflow, or the taxonomies it aligns to.
in_scope: Position identity, keys, official and working titles, and language-tagged alternative labels
Assigned duties, responsibilities and essential functions attributed to the position rather than to an incumbent
Occupational classification, job/class membership, grade or level and job-evaluation outcome
Placement in an organizational unit, cost centre, reporting and supervisory structure
Work location, work arrangement and schedule attributes attached to the seat
Capacity and occupancy control: FTE, headcount, single vs pooled, overlap tolerance, vacancy state
Budget, funding source and the pay range or grade ladder framing the seat
Qualification, competency, credential, screening, clearance and approval requirements
Delegated decision rights and externally prescribed regulatory responsibilities allocated to the seat
Lifecycle states, effective-dated versioning, classification authority, certification, appeal and retention
out_of_scope: The natural person, worker or agent identity that may occupy the position
The occupancy relationship itself (appointment, assignment, tenure, occupancy dates) — owned by WM-ORG-016
The organizational unit as an entity, its charter and its own hierarchy — owned by WM-ORG-002
Team formation and team-level goals — owned by WM-ORG-003
Employment contract terms, payroll processing, absence and time records
Recruiting workflow: requisition approval chain, candidate pipeline, interview and selection records
The occupation, skill and competency taxonomies themselves (ISCO-08, ESCO, O*NET-SOC, NICE) — referenced, not owned
Individual performance appraisal, development plans and remuneration paid to an incumbent
Compensation plan and pay-structure master data (grade ladders and steps are referenced by key)

boundary_notes.distinction: The position persists while vacant; the assignment exists only while an agent occupies it. W3C separates org:Post (independent of holder) from org:Membership, which exists only when an agent occupies a role. Occupancy dates, tenure and incumbent-specific terms belong to the assignment, not the position.

A unit is a collection of people and functions with its own recognition inside a larger organization; a position is a single seat that is contained in exactly one unit at a time via org:postIn / org:hasPost. Unit charter, mandate and unit hierarchy stay with WM-ORG-002.

A position is an instance; a class is 'all positions which are sufficiently similar as to kind of work, level of difficulty and responsibility, and qualification requirements' (5 CFR 511.101), and an occupation is 'a set of jobs whose main tasks and duties are characterised by a high degree of similarity' (ISCO-08). Classifier definitions, code lists and hierarchies are external registries; the position holds only the coded reference and the evaluation evidence.

A vacancy notice is a published recruiting artifact with its own validity window, datePosted, validThrough and application channel; it is a projection referencing zero, one or many positions. HR Open keeps PositionOpening in the recruiting domain and organizational structure with incumbents in OrganizationChart.

W3C org:Role denotes the abstract role and requires a Membership instance to link a person, whereas org:Post is a concrete organizational seat. Role vocabularies (NICE work roles, ESCO occupations) are alignments, not the position itself.

Pay range, grade ladder and budget frame the seat; actual remuneration, contractual clauses and payroll results attach to the occupant's employment relation. EU pay-transparency duties bind the employer's disclosure at recruitment and reporting, not the position record's internal semantics.

functions.name: Specify requirements and essential functions
functions.description: Record essential and marginal functions, competencies, credentials and experience required of any holder, using versioned catalogue references.
preconditions: duties are decomposed at task granularity
catalogue versions are pinned
analysis is authored before advertising or interviewing
effects: requirements become auditable evidence for selection and accommodation decisions

functions.name: Allocate authority and prescribed responsibilities
functions.description: Confer decision rights on the seat and allocate any regulator-prescribed responsibilities to it without leaving gaps.
preconditions: the position is sufficiently senior for the responsibilities
gap analysis across the firm has been performed
effects: accountability is attributable to a designated seat independent of turnover
vacancy behaviour for each delegation is defined

functions.name: Designate risk and screening requirements
functions.description: Determine the clearance, vetting, regulatory approval and access requirements that attach to the seat before recruitment starts.
inputs: access entitlements implied by the duties
outputs: position risk and screening designation record
preconditions: duties and access entitlements are known
the applicable regime is identified for the seat's jurisdiction
effects: recruitment and provisioning can enforce prerequisites
lapse handling rules become executable

functions.name: Reconcile occupancy and vacancy
functions.description: Compute consumed and open capacity from assignment records and validate incoming occupancy against the authorization.
inputs: current assignment references and consumed capacity
preconditions: assignment records are readable from the occupancy model
capacity authorization is current at the as-of date
effects: vacancy is derived rather than asserted
capacity breaches are warned or blocked per the overlap flag

functions.name: Amend or reclassify position
functions.description: Apply an effective-dated change to duties, placement, capacity or classification, distinguishing correction from substantive change.
outputs: re-issued description or evaluation where triggered
preconditions: authorizing party holds the relevant authority
effective date does not silently overwrite prior versions
effects: prior versions remain queryable as of their effective windows
dependent artifacts are flagged for review

functions.name: Certify description and process appeals
functions.description: Certify the accuracy of the position description and administer challenges to its classification, applying decision effective dates.
outputs: corrected classification with its effective date
preconditions: the description states the duties actually assigned
the appellant and the matter are within scope of appeal
effects: the record becomes evidentiary
corrected classifications take effect on their own governed date

functions.name: Publish position projection
functions.description: Generate an outbound projection of the position for a named recipient profile, applying suppression rules and disclosure duties.
outputs: pay range disclosure record where required
preconditions: position is in an approved status for staffing projections
required pay-range disclosure has been determined for the jurisdiction
effects: downstream systems and the public receive a governed subset
disclosure evidence is retained

functions.name: Freeze, abolish or dispose position
functions.description: Move the seat to frozen or abolished status and, at the end of retention, apply the governed disposition action to its records.
preconditions: occupancy preconditions are satisfied or explicitly overridden
no preservation hold is active before disposition
effects: the seat stops consuming establishment and budget
history is preserved until retention expiry, then disposed with an auditable record

functions.name: Authorize fill or freeze
functions.description: Permit or withhold recruitment against a vacant Position, producing a fill-authorization that a JobPosting or requisition may reference.
preconditions: Position is established and not abolished.
Classification and PD are adequate if the local regime requires them before advertisement.
effects: A JobPosting may be linked as an advertisement of this vacancy; the posting is not the Position.
Freeze withholds fill without abolishing the slot.

composition.purpose: Every position is contained in exactly one organizational unit at a given effective date, matching org:postIn / org:hasPost and the mandatory department reference in production position records.
Teams are composed through positions and their assignments; positions remain reusable across team formations and are referenced, not owned, by the team model.

A position is occupied through a scoped assignment; occupancy, tenure and incumbent-specific terms live there, mirroring the org:Post versus org:Membership separation, and supply the consumed capacity used to derive vacancy.

composition.target: Job / class / occupation classifier model (sibling; registry entry not yet identified)
composition.purpose: The class grouping similar positions and the occupational category are external classifier concepts; the position holds only coded references, not the class definitions or hierarchies.

composition.target: Person / worker identity model (sibling; registry entry not yet identified)
composition.purpose: Incumbents are referenced only indirectly through assignments so that the position record carries no personal data of its own.
Alignment target for occupational coding and for the job-versus-occupation distinction; mapping strength and version are recorded and conformance is not claimed without assessment evidence.
Alignment target for multilingual labels, scope notes, regulatory aspects and essential or optional skills at ISCO level 5 and below.
Alignment target for duty decomposition into work activities, for requirement typing and for environmental work-context descriptors.
Ontological alignment for publishing positions as graph nodes with postIn, heldBy and reportsTo edges, and for the vacancy-independent semantics of a post.

composition.target: HR Open Standards 4.5 (OrganizationChart, PositionOpening, PositionCompetencyModel, HRMasterData)
composition.purpose: Exchange alignment for organizational structure, recruiting projections, competency models and provisioning payloads.
Publication alignment for the advertisement projection only; the posting is a time-bounded document about the position, not the position itself.

composition.target: NICE Workforce Framework work roles (NIST SP 800-181 Rev.1)
composition.purpose: Alignment for composing Task, Knowledge and Skill statements into reusable requirement sets that organizations map onto positions.
Supplies the bitemporal pattern separating business effective windows from RFC 3339 record and observation instants, reused by every attribute group in this model.
Adds prescribed responsibility allocation, statements of responsibilities and responsibilities maps for positions in regulated firms without imposing them on all adopters.
Adds statutory class, grade, official position description certification, classification appeal and effective-date rules for public-sector adopters bound by such a plan.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must name one owner package that is master for position identity, declare the master system of record, and state whether position codes are unique globally or only within a business unit.

The owner package must publish who holds establishment authority, who holds classification authority and which approvals gate the proposed-to-approved transition, since the definition of a position depends on assignment by competent authority.
The owner package must register every external scheme it maps to, pin the scheme version in use, and maintain the crosswalk table with mapping strength and recorded conflicts.
The owner package must declare the retention and disposition schedule for position records and artifacts, and the personal-data boundary that keeps incumbent data in the assignment model.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use one namespace per Dimension and per master system, for example vr:wm-org-004/{dimension}/{master-system}/position/{position-key}. Publish a resolvable IRI per position when the organization graph is exposed, typed as org:Post. Never encode title, grade, unit or date into the identifier, because all four are effective-dated and mutable; codes may appear in a separate human-facing position code field whose uniqueness scope is declared.
registry_links: vr.wm-org-004 (this entry; nav path NAV.SOC.ORG.POS)
planning/VERCY-MODEL-RELATIONS.csv for CONTAINS from WM-ORG-002, COMPOSE from WM-ORG-003 and COMPOSE to WM-ORG-016
External registries referenced by pinned version: ISCO-08, ESCO occupations, O*NET-SOC, NICE work roles, HR Open Standards 4.5

canonicalization_rules: The canonical form is a format-neutral record; JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB are encodings that must round-trip the same canonical content.
Every coded value is stored as a scheme, version and code triple; a bare label is never canonical and never sufficient for a classification assertion.
Every label carries a language tag; the official title is distinguished from working and alternative labels by an explicit label role.
All instants are RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; business effective dates may be full-date values and are held in fields distinct from record instants.
Collections are ordered deterministically by a stable key so that content hashes are reproducible across systems.
patch_rules: Changes to duty content, classification, grade, capacity, funding or authority create a new effective-dated version; in-place mutation of a closed version is prohibited.
Every patch declares its effective date, its change type as correction or substantive change, a governed reason code and the authorizing party.
Corrections restate what the record should always have said and must preserve the erroneous version with a superseding marker; substantive changes open a new business validity window.
Deletion of history is prohibited; a position is ended by closing its effective window and recording an abolition decision, and records leave only through governed disposition at retention expiry.
A patch that changes classification must carry the classification action effective date separately from the decision instant, since the two are governed differently.
compatibility_rules: Adding optional attributes or new crosswalk entries is a minor change; changing identity semantics, uniqueness scope, capacity units or a pinned scheme version is breaking.
Consumers must tolerate unknown codes and unknown optional fields rather than rejecting the record.
Re-versioning an external scheme requires an explicit re-mapping decision with its own instant; silent code carry-over across scheme versions is prohibited.
Derived values such as vacancy state must never be treated as stable inputs by consumers; they are valid only for the as-of instant at which they were computed.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system position identifier assigned by the HRIS or position-control system of record.
Governed global identifier or resolvable IRI, such as the org:Post IRI published in the organization graph.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension only where no upstream authoritative identifier exists, recorded together with the reason no upstream key was available.
Never an identifier: official or working title, grade, unit, cost centre, incumbent name, or any date.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All instants use RFC 3339 date-time with seconds and an explicit offset or Z, per the Internet date/time profile of ISO 8601; -00:00 is used only for the unknown-local-offset case and is not equivalent to Z. Event time, business effective date and observation or ingestion instant are recorded in separate fields and never conflated.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named wm-org-004--{dimension}--{position-key}--{artifact-kind}--{effective-or-instant}--v{n}, lower-kebab-case throughout, with the instant in RFC 3339 basic-safe form so that lexical order equals chronological order. Version numbers increase monotonically and are never reused after disposition.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Each serial artifact records a content hash over its canonical serialization plus the identity of the certifying or authorizing party. Certified position descriptions, evaluation statements, statements of responsibilities and appeal decisions are immutable once certified; any change produces a new version that references the hash of the version it supersedes.

policies: Position records must remain occupant-free: no attribute of a position may identify a natural person, because a post exists independently of the person or persons filling it and occupancy belongs to the assignment model.

Single occupancy must never be assumed. Concurrency is governed explicitly by position type, headcount and the overlap-allowed flag, since both the ontology and production systems permit a post to be held by more than one holder.
A position may not be advertised or staffed until its classification, requirements, risk and screening designation and any pay-range disclosure duty have been determined and recorded.

External standards are alignments, not conformance claims; a conformance assertion requires named assessment evidence with a method and date, and unresolved disagreements between schemes are recorded rather than silently resolved.
Derived state such as vacancy is computed, timestamped and never persisted as an independent assertion that could diverge from its inputs.
Classification, grade, pay-range and risk-designation fields are governed reads: access is role-scoped and every read of pay or sensitivity data is logged.
A Position may be created, classified, frozen, published and abolished without an occupant.
Occupant personal data, actual salary and tenure live on assignment records; access and retention of those fields follow privacy law, not the PD schedule.
Public official Posts may publish label, organization, area and vacancy while withholding HR evaluation content.
Reclassification, abolishment and fill-freeze are privileged operations with named competent authorities and audit.

read: Read a position as of a business effective date, returning the version whose effective window contains that date together with its record instants.
Read the change history of a position, including superseded versions, change types and reason codes.
Read derived occupancy and open capacity for an as-of instant, with the assignment references that were consulted.
Read outbound projections filtered by payload profile and by the suppression rules applicable to the recipient class.
create: Create a position only through the establish function, with duties assigned by a named competent authority and a holding unit reference present.
Mint the identifier under the owner package namespace following the identity priority order and record the assignment instant.
Create derived artifacts such as evaluation statements, designations and certifications as new serial versions, never as edits.
update: Update only by appending a new effective-dated version carrying effective date, change type, reason code and authorizing party.
Update classification only through the classification authority, recording the classification action effective date separately from the decision instant.
Update capacity or funding only with the corresponding authorization artifact present.
Reject updates that would place personal data of an incumbent on the position record.
delete: Hard deletion of position records or their history is prohibited while any retention period or preservation hold applies.
End a position by closing its effective window and recording an abolition decision with its effective date; the identifier is retired and not reused.
Dispose records only at retention expiry, by the governed disposition action, with an auditable disposition record naming the approving role and the RFC 3339 instant.
Erasure requests concerning a person are satisfied in the assignment or worker model, not by deleting the position.

roles.name: Position owner (competent authority)
responsibilities: Assign and revise the duties and responsibilities that constitute the position
Authorize establishment, freeze, reinstatement and abolition decisions
Certify that the position description states the duties actually assigned

roles.name: Classification and evaluation authority
responsibilities: Place the position in a class and assign occupational codes with pinned scheme versions
Apply objective, gender-neutral evaluation criteria and record criterion ratings
Maintain consistency across comparable positions and administer redetermination after appeals

roles.name: Position control and budget steward
responsibilities: Authorize FTE, headcount, position type and overlap tolerance
Bind the seat to budget and funding source and manage funding lapse handling
Reconcile establishment counts, open capacity and budget reporting

roles.name: Model data steward
responsibilities: Own the identifier namespace, uniqueness scope and crosswalk tables
Enforce canonicalization, patch and retention rules and run validation suites
Maintain the evidence ledger, integrity hashes and conflict records

roles.name: Compliance and regulatory officer
responsibilities: Allocate prescribed responsibilities without gaps and maintain statements of responsibilities and the responsibilities map
Determine risk, screening, clearance and approval prerequisites for the seat
Determine jurisdictional pay-transparency and reporting duties and retain disclosure evidence

roles.name: Consuming agent
responsibilities: Read positions as of a stated effective date and honour pinned scheme versions
Treat derived state as valid only for its as-of instant and tolerate unknown codes and optional fields
Never infer classification, exemption status or authority from a title alone

access.default_rule: Position structural data is internal to the organization by default and readable by authenticated organizational agents at bundle and layer scope; pay, evaluation, risk, screening and authority data are restricted to named roles, and no scope grants access to identifiable incumbent data, which is governed by the assignment model.
exceptions: Published vacancy projections are public for their publication window and expose only the fields permitted by the payload profile.
Pay range must be disclosed to applicants prior to employment where the jurisdiction requires it, overriding the default restriction on pay data for that audience and purpose.
Aggregate pay information by category of workers is disclosable to workers and to regulators under pay-transparency and reporting duties, in aggregate form only.
Statements of responsibilities and responsibilities maps are disclosable to the relevant regulator on request, including superseded versions.
Risk, sensitivity and clearance designations are restricted to compliance, security and staffing roles and are excluded from public and general internal projections.
Preservation holds override retention-driven disposition and suspend deletion until the hold is lifted.
Public-office transparency for elected or gazette Posts.
Named audit or legal-hold access to historical PDs.
Emergency fill against a vacant essential Position under recorded authority.
Unnamed FHIR-style clinical slots may expose service and location without a person.
audit_requirements: Log every classification, evaluation, capacity, funding, authority and status decision with the actor identity, the decision instant in RFC 3339 and the separately recorded effective date.
Log every read of pay-range, evaluation-criterion, risk-designation and screening fields with the reader identity, purpose and instant.
Log every outbound projection with its payload profile, recipient class, suppression rules applied, content hash and generation instant.
Log overlap and capacity-validation outcomes, including warnings, blocks and any override with the overriding authority.
Log disposition actions and preservation holds with approving role and instant, and retain the log beyond the disposition of the records it describes.
Record who classified, certified, froze, authorized fill, abolished or hard-deleted a Position, with event time and ingestion time.
Record access to occupant-derived views and to sensitivity-coded Positions.
Retain audit independently of occupant PII deletion.
